title: Probability of returning no bit
statement: Let $\rho$ be any real number and let $K$ be a natural number. For $2K$ independent bits, each equal to true with probability $\rho$, the rule that examines consecutive pairs, discards equal pairs, and returns the first bit of the first unequal pair returns no bit with probability $(\rho^2+(1-\rho)^2)^K$.
hypotheses_covered: $\rho$ is a real number, with no further restriction
